subject: Safelist validation runbook for private connectors / next steps
messages:
From: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudOps <cloudops@orbitalhealth.com>, Infra Security <infra-security@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private connector safelist — validation & runbook request

Hannah,

Thanks for taking this on. We are nearing the integration window for Redwood's private connector and need to validate our safelist approach before we move to staging. Two asks from my team: (1) a short runbook we can use during cutover to validate outbound connectivity and firewall rules, and (2) a definitive list of what destinations/ports to allow for the control plane and telemetry (we will enforce on our perimeter firewall + proxy).

Current environment notes: On-prem VPC, outbound egress via centralized NAT gateway, TLS inspection enabled on the perimeter (we can create exceptions if required), and a corporate HTTP proxy for non-https traffic.

Can you confirm what our ops team will need to open (IPs + ports / hostnames + ports / DNS exceptions) and whether Redwood expects any long-lived inbound connectivity from your side? Also attaching our standard "IP exception" form in case we need an approval trail.

Appreciate a pragmatic runbook — checklist style — that our SREs can follow.

-Matt
Infra Security / Orbital Health
[Attachment: ip-exception-request-form.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector safelist — validation & runbook request

Matt — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (Solutions) and Vanessa (Network/Field Ops) so we can produce a short, operational runbook and a verified destination list. A few quick clarifying items that will change the allowlist we provide:

- Will you permit TLS pass-through for connections to our control plane hostnames, or will TLS be terminated/inspected? If inspection will remain in-line we may need to provide certs/keys for mutual TLS or suggest hostname-based bypasses for the inspection appliance.
- Do you enforce outbound port whitelisting beyond 443/853? (some customers only allow 443, others permit 53/853 for DNS, 123 for NTP, 443 for HTTPS, 443/tcp for websockets, and a small ephemeral range for metadata calls).
- Do you have an internal HTTP proxy that all outbound traffic breaks through? If so, do you prefer we list hostnames for the proxy to forward to, or do you need public IP ranges for firewall rules at the perimeter?

We will draft a checklist-runbook with: pre-cutover validations, DNS lookup checks, certificate validation steps, NAT mapping verification, and post-cutover telemetry verifications. I'll get a first pass over by EOD tomorrow.

Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: safelist-validation-runbook-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector safelist — validation & runbook request

Folks — attaching the first-pass runbook. High level summary of what Redwood expects (we will confirm exact IPs after control plane maintenance later this week):

- Outbound TLS to controlplane.redwood-inference.com over 443 (we recommend hostname allow and/or the IP ranges listed below).
- DNS: allow egress to whatever internal resolver is used; we suggest allowing recursive DNS to 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4 or your corporate resolver; if DNS TLS is used, port 853 should be available.
- NTP: outbound UDP 123 for time drift checks (important for cert validation).
- Websockets / streaming: 443/tcp (same host) — Redwood streams over standard HTTPS, no additional ports needed.
- Telemetry / metrics: HTTPS to telemetry-collector.redwood-inference.com over 443. We will provide a signed certificate for mutual TLS if you enable mTLS on the perimeter.

Temporary allowances we sometimes see customers need during cutover: 1) an ephemeral NAT binding review window so SRE can validate public IP egress mapping, 2) a short-lived exception to TLS inspection for control plane hostnames. Both are optional but speed troubleshooting.

Planned IP ranges to be validated (subject to change, will confirm final list):
- 18.132.0.0/20
- 34.76.128.0/18
- 52.211.16.0/20

We will not request any inbound firewall openings to your network — Redwood never initiates inbound sessions into customer private connectors.

Marissa
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector safelist — validation & runbook request

Matt / Orbital team — quick ops notes from the field:

1) If you run TLS inspection, consider creating a hostname bypass for controlplane.redwood-inference.com and telemetry-collector.redwood-inference.com instead of adding a cert-level exception. That keeps inspection rules intact for other traffic.

2) For NAT validation: run the following from a test host behind your NAT gateway during the window:
   - curl -v https://controlplane.redwood-inference.com/health 
   - curl --resolve controlplane.redwood-inference.com:443:<expected_public_ip> https://controlplane.redwood-inference.com/health 
   - dig +short controlplane.redwood-inference.com @<your-resolver>

3) If you use an egress proxy, configure it to allow CONNECT to the Redwood hostnames on 443; do not attempt TLS interception for connection streams (it breaks our websocket streaming). If you must inspect, we can provide mTLS certs for mutual auth — opens an approval track but is supported.

4) DNS caching: ensure your DNS TTLs are honored for quick rollbacks during failover. We'll coordinate change windows to keep TTLs low for cutover days.

I'll coordinate with your CloudOps point of contact to carve out a 2-hour validation window next week.

Vanessa
Field Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector safelist — validation & runbook request

All — thanks for the checklist and notes. We ran the pre-cutover checks this morning in our dev pod and everything behaved as described except one item: our perimeter proxy blocks CONNECT for websocket upgrades even when destination is allowed. CloudOps will look at a proxy rule exception for the validation window.

Next steps we agreed internally:
- CloudOps will open a temporary proxy rule to allow Connect with upgraded handshake to the Redwood hostnames for a 2-hour window next Wed at 02:00 UTC.
- I will submit the IP exception form for the temporary NAT public IP audit trail if needed.
- Hannah / Marissa: please send a final signed list of IP ranges after your maintenance window so we can lock firewall policy before prod cutover.

Appreciate the help.

Matt
Infra Security / Orbital Health
